anna: quick idea — instead of a server-side shim for the v3->v4 request shape, what about an SDK-side transform pipeline we can ship as a compatibility experiment for ~6 weeks? avoids extra proxy hops and lets client versions opt-in. thoughts?

derek: hmm interesting. main win is less runtime load on gateway, right? also pushes logic to SDK owners which could fragment behavior. :thinking:

maria: from SDK side this is fairly straightforward — we already have middleware hooks. we can add a small transform that rewrites body/headers for old call sites and emits telemetry. example: ```js
// in sdk middleware order
sdk.transforms.push(req => {
  if (req.headers['x-rw-client-version'] && req.headers['x-rw-client-version'].startsWith('3')) {
    // normalize v3 -> v4 shape
    req.body = { prompt: req.body.input, options: req.body.opts }
    req.headers['x-rw-compat-migrated'] = 'sdk-v3->v4'
  }
  return req
})
```

leo: infra questions — how will we measure coverage? we need a reliable way to know what % of production traffic is still hitting transformed paths. plus security review: SDK changing request shapes could affect auth/masking.

maria: plan is to add a telemetry beacon when a transform runs: header + post-event to telemetry ingest with a hashed tenant id. opt-in by default for early releases, then enable for all SDK users after notice. header example: `x-rw-compat-report: 1`

compat-bot: deploy note — any SDK-side rollouts still need release artifacts recorded in the change-log channel.

anna: tradeoffs doc sketch:
- pros: reduces gateway CPU, faster iteration (we can quickly iterate per-language), easy rollback (release new SDK), preserves server backwards compatibility without maintaining a shim forever.
- cons: fragmentation risk, some customers bypass SDKs (curl/own clients), extra test surface in SDKs.

derek: for non-SDK traffic we still need a minimal server fallback. I'd suggest a thin, best-effort fallback that only handles the most common diffs (body rename, header mapping) and returns 422 with a clear migration hint when it can't reconcile. that keeps burden low.

maria: agreed — SDK first, gateway minimal fallback. we can gate the SDK transform behind a feature flag so we can A/B test error rates and quality impact. the flag should be remote-config so we can flip per-tenant.

leo: ops-wise we'll want these signals: transform_count, transform_success_rate, transform_fallbacks_count (when gateway fallback invoked), latency_delta_ms. add a tag for tenant and sdk-language. keep PII out (hash tenant ids).

anna: rollout proposal:
1) RFC + brief to support + security (this thread) — this week
2) SDK implement + telemetry + feature flag — next 2 weeks (maria)
3) Canary SDK release to 10% of active users, feature-flag off by default — collect metrics 1 week
4) Enable flag for more users while keeping gateway minimal fallback — 2 weeks
5) Decide on server shim removal or keep minimal fallback permanently (metrics-driven) — end of experiment (~6 weeks)

derek: sounds reasonable. need a clear abort criteria: if transform_success_rate < 98% or error rate increases by >0.5% we roll back. also monitor tail latency increase per tenant.

maria: will add a small test harness in SDK e2e tests to validate transform idempotence and that we don't double-wrap requests.

leo: security: we'll run a quick threat model. main risk is header spoofing of `x-rw-compat-migrated` — gateway should not trust that header for auth decisions, only for telemetry. also make sure transformations don't introduce new sensitive fields into logs.

anna: action items:
- maria: prototype transform + telemetry + feature-flag (due in 10 working days)
- derek: implement minimal gateway fallback (best-effort mapper + helpful 422) (due in 2 weeks)
- leo: add metrics/alerts template and run threat model (due in 1 week)
- anna: write short RFC and coordinate ops/security sign-off (due EOW)

maria: noted. I'll open PRs with feature-flag and telemetry events and ping this channel.

derek: i'll stub the fallback endpoint and share mapping heuristics.

anna: cool, thanks. this approach should give us a low-friction path to migrate callers while keeping the server safe. :shipit:

compat-bot: reminder — please add release checklist entries when SDK artifacts are published.
